title: Why did Android replace Makefiles with Android.bp?

cast.name: Mia
cast.role: Tooling dev who wants answers without running a build

cast.name: Dev
cast.role: Build veteran who has debugged every Makefile

glossary.note: Go code that turns Android.bp into Ninja rules.

glossary.full: The parser library Soong is built on

key_points: Android.mk is make code you must run to understand; Android.bp is declarative data.
Soong turns Android.bp into build.ninja, and mutators clone modules into variants.
Make is more flexible; Blueprint is faster to parse and analyze.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Same tiny program, two build files. Mia's tool has to list what each one builds, without running a build.

beats.speaker: mia
beats.say: Exhibit A: the old Android dot M K.

beats.speaker: dev
beats.text: That's GNU make. The ifeq is code, so you only learn what gets built by running it.
beats.say: That's G N U make. The if E Q is code, so you only learn what gets built by running it.

beats.speaker: mia
beats.text: So to list modules, I'd execute thousands of these. Every build does exactly that.

beats.speaker: dev
beats.say: Exhibit B: Android dot B P.

beats.speaker: mia
beats.text: No loops. No if. Just a module type and properties.

beats.speaker: dev
beats.text: A parser reads it like data. Per-architecture differences are just nested properties.

beats.speaker: mia
beats.text: So where does the build logic live?

beats.speaker: dev
beats.text: In Go. The Blueprint library parses every Android.bp, and Soong defines module types like cc_binary.
beats.say: In Go. The Blueprint library parses every Android dot B P, and Soong defines module types like C C binary.

beats.speaker: dev
beats.text: Soong writes out/soong/build.ninja, and Ninja runs it.
beats.say: Soong writes out slash soong slash build dot ninja, and Ninja runs it.

beats.speaker: mia
beats.text: But the phone needs arm64 and arm builds of hello.
beats.say: But the phone needs arm sixty-four and arm builds of hello.

beats.speaker: dev
beats.text: Mutators clone each module into variants: architecture, core or vendor, shared or static.

beats.speaker: dev
beats.text: Need arbitrary logic per file? Make wins. Need a fast graph a tool can read? Blueprint wins.

beats.speaker: mia
beats.text: Then my tool reads Android.bp as plain data, and never runs it.
beats.say: Then my tool reads Android dot B P as plain data, and never runs it.
